headline: Three Former Chief Justices Argue Impeachment Conviction Threshold Should Track Eligible, Participating Senators
seoTitle: Former Chief Justices Weigh In on Sara Duterte Impeachment Vote Threshold | FMB News
seoDescription: Artemio Panganiban, Hilario Davide Jr. and Reynato Puno told the Senate impeachment court that the conviction threshold should not automatically be fixed at 16 votes from a 24-member base.
deck: The legal advisers' positions are recommendations to the Senate impeachment court, not a ruling. Senator-judges are expected to resolve the disputed computation after further proceedings.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Three retired Supreme Court chief justices advising the Senate impeachment court said Wednesday that the two-thirds conviction requirement in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial should be computed from senators who are legally qualified and meaningfully participating, rather than automatically treating 16 votes out of 24 as an immutable number.

GMA News reported the positions of retired Chief Justices Artemio Panganiban, Hilario Davide Jr. and Reynato Puno during Day 26 of the proceedings. Their views were presented as amici curiae, or friends of the court, and do not themselves change the court's existing rule.

sections.heading: What the advisers said
paragraphs: Panganiban argued that active participation and independent evaluation of the evidence are necessary to discharge a senator-judge's constitutional responsibility. Davide's written memorandum said the denominator should be senators qualified to vote and should not automatically include members legally unable to participate. Puno likewise rejected treating 16 as fixed solely from the Senate's nominal 24-member composition.

Puno also argued that the Senate impeachment court is not subordinate to the Supreme Court in the same manner as ordinary courts. These are legal positions offered to the impeachment court, not final judicial holdings in this proceeding.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: The Senate impeachment court has not yet issued its final resolution on the disputed voting base. The position of each senator-judge, and the final number required to sustain or overturn the existing threshold ruling, remain matters for the court's formal action.

Retired Associate Justice Adolfo Azcuna also participated as an amicus curiae. FMB News is not attributing a specific position to him in this update beyond what has been independently verified in the cited reporting.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Presiding officer Francis Escudero earlier ruled that conviction requires 16 affirmative votes, based on two-thirds of the Senate's full 24-member composition. Questions later arose over how to treat senator-judges who are absent or legally unable to participate.

The House prosecution and Duterte defense remain opposing parties in the impeachment case. The allegations against Duterte are contested and have not been finally adjudicated by the Senate impeachment court.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The threshold determines how the Constitution's two-thirds requirement will operate in a Senate whose full nominal membership and actual participating membership are not identical. The procedural ruling can therefore affect the mechanics of the eventual verdict without deciding the merits of the impeachment allegations themselves.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the completion of the amici presentations, the September 23 oral arguments announced by the impeachment court, and the senator-judges' formal vote on the threshold issue. FMB News will report the court's actual ruling separately when issued.

verificationNotes: GMA News' live report was updated at 1:17 p.m. PHT and directly reports the positions of Panganiban, Davide and Puno.
Inquirer independently reported Davide's position on computing the threshold from senators qualified to vote.

A House of Representatives press release confirms that the impeachment court heard differing interpretations from four retired Supreme Court justices and that the prosecution treats the threshold as unresolved.
The article carefully describes the amici positions as advisory legal views, not a Senate ruling.
The allegations in the underlying impeachment case remain contested and are not presented as established facts.
The hero is a Philippine News Agency photograph of the Senate session hall hosted on Wikimedia Commons and marked public domain in the Philippines; it is explicitly labeled as a file image.
